title: Two college cyclists killed, seven injured after driver strikes team in Tennessee
content:
Two members of the Milligan University cycling team were killed and seven others were injured, and a driver was charged with vehicular homicide on Wednesday after officials said he struck riders who were training on a mountain highway in Tennessee.

Sophomores Brayden Rogers and Haylan Engdahl were killed in the crash, which happened around 8 a.m., according to Milligan, a private Christian liberal arts school in northeastern Tennessee, near Johnson City. The crash occurred on Highway 19E near Simerly Creek Road in Carter County, the Tennessee Highway Patrol said on social media.

The driver, John Benfield, 69, of Newland, N.C., has been charged with two counts of vehicular homicide by recklessness and five counts of aggravated assault by vehicle by recklessness, Steven R. Finney, the district attorney general for Carter County, said at a news conference. Benfield was booked into jail.

“It is more important than ever right now that we are a community gathered around Jesus and we need Jesus deeply,” Stephen Waers, the president of Milligan, said in a YouTube video. “I’d like to invite you into prayer with us, into grief with us, into prayer for the families of those we have lost, into prayer for those who are still receiving treatment.”

Seven of the school’s 11 cyclists were taken to Johnson City Medical Center to receive care, according to Waers. Authorities did not release further information on their condition.

Tennessee Highway Patrol Maj. Roy Brown said at the news conference that a large number of emergency workers responded to the crash, including multiple air medical teams transporting injured people for treatment. Brown said the crash remains under investigation.

“We know the families, the Milligan community and people across this region want answers,” the Tennessee Highway Patrol said in a statement. “We want those answers too. Our responsibility now is to conduct a careful and thorough investigation and provide information based on the facts.”

Finney said officials will reach out to the families of the victims to organize a group meeting so they can receive the “answers that we can give” regarding the case. He added that Milligan, with an enrollment of around 1,200 students, had an “elite cycling team.”

In May, Milligan’s cycling team claimed the men’s team time trial national title at the USA Cycling Collegiate Road Nationals in Madison, Wis.

“It’s not a bunch of those club guys getting together to ride,” Finney said. “They know what they’re doing. They rode in a peloton. One of the boys just won last weekend in one of the local races.”

“I want the media to know, and I want our community to know that these young men chose to come here, chose to come to this school, and they are members of our community as such,” he added. “You should treat them with the grace and the dignity — and their families — that they deserve.”
